## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Fix case-insensitive writes before merge. A mixed-case key written through the new API cannot be read back.

## Changes

The pull request adds `Cache.set`, raises the default TTL from 60 to 300 seconds, and adds tests for lookups and expiry.

## Critical

- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Normalize keys before storing them — After `set("Alpha", 1)`, `get("Alpha")` returns `None` because `set` stores `"Alpha"` and `get` looks up `"alpha"`. — Callers using mixed-case keys get cache misses immediately after a successful write.

## Important

- tests/test_cache.py:27 — tests — Verify the entry can be read before expiry — With `ttl=1`, an implementation that expires the entry immediately passes `test_entries_expire` because the test first reads it two seconds after writing it. — The test can pass even when callers never get a cache hit during the configured lifetime.

## Suggestions

- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Expire entries at the TTL deadline — If `set` writes an entry at time `1000.0` with `ttl=1`, `get` returns it at `1001.0` because the expiry check uses a strict less-than comparison. — A lookup at the deadline can return stale data after the configured TTL has elapsed. — Fix: Use `expires <= time.monotonic()` at `app/cache.py:21`.
- app/cache.py:7 — comments — Identify 300 seconds as the default TTL — For `Cache(ttl=1)`, the comment says “Entries expire 300 seconds after they are written,” but `set` computes the deadline with `time.monotonic() + self._ttl`. — The comment gives callers using a custom TTL the wrong retention period.
